entries.title: Isaiah 20:1
segments: Tartan; a general that served under both Sargoan and Sennacherib.

Sargon; probably the immediate successor of Sennacherib. 
 
  Ashdod; a strong fortress in Philistia.  It lay on the road to Egypt, and its capture opened the way for an attack on that country. 
 
The expectations of all who forsake the living God, and the way of salvation which he has provided, to put their trust in man or any thing that man can do, shall end in disappointment and ruin.

entries.title: Isaiah 20:2
segments: Sackcloth; probably a coarse garment which was worn as a badge of the prophetic office.
Naked; that is, comparatively naked, without his garment of sackcloth and shoes.
This was a sign of the condition in which the Egyptian and Ethiopian captives should be led away.

entries.title: Isaiah 20:5
segments: They; the Jews, who are often rebuked for putting their trust in Egypt.

entries.title: Isaiah 20:6
segments:
This isle; or, "this country," or coast; the Mediterranean coast, which included the land of Judea. 
 
  Such is our expectation; such is its issue; it has ended in disappointment. 
 
  Whither we flee for help; that is, from Egypt, wihther we have fled for help.
